Current Non-Fungible Tokens are constrained by limitations related to single-transaction rewards and product silos. Since creators cease to earn additional benefits after an initial sale due to a disconnect across diverse NFTs, disputes over future profit distribution often arise. To address these issues and ensure long-term incentives, we propose a referability NFT framework. This approach utilizes a referable Non-Fungible Token (rNFT) network designed to expand market reach by strengthening referral linkages among complementary items. By implementing Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) logic, we establish weighted, labeled directed relationships between NFT pairs. Our implementation adheres to Ethereum standards—specifically indexing under the multi-asset token standard EIP-1155—and provides mathematical derivations to evaluate the utility of each participant. Offering broad guidance on multiple parameters, this research delivers, to our knowledge, an initial analysis explicitly constructing and visualizing the virtual interconnectivity within a referability NFT ecosystem.

Although host star activities are recognized as a major factor influencing the habitability of their planetary systems, coronal mass ejections (CMEs) remain elusive and are seldom detected around solar-like and late-type stars. This observational study utilizes high-cadence data from the Ground Wide-angle Camera to examine flares occurring on two M-dwarfs, utilizing the resulting fast, time-resolved spectroscopy to characterize them consistently. Both detections revealed symmetric broad Hα emission profiles featuring minimal bulk velocity alongside significant projected maximum velocities reaching approximately 700–79 km s−1. This extreme broadening is likely attributable to either stellar pressure effects or fast-moving mass outflows at the stellar surface resembling CMEs; within a CME framework, inferred masses for these events range from $\sim4\times10^{18}$g to $2\times10^{19}$g. Additionally, variability in the central line velocity of the narrow Hα component was identified in the spectra for both instances, with shifts of tens km s−1 potentialy arising from either chromospheric ejections in the first case and gravitational forces due to binary interaction in the second. Finally, by coupling total flaring energy measurements derived from our photometry with the mass estimates, we demonstrate a clear correlation indicating that higher flare energies are linked to significantly larger ejected masses.

This study introduces a straightforward qualitative model to elucidate the shear rheological behavior of twist-bend nematic liquid crystals. Our findings indicate an initial decrease in effective viscosity with shear rate at low rates, characteristic of shear-thinning behavior. This trend transitions into an approximate stress plateau independent of the shear rate at intermediate rates, eventually shifting to a Newtonian rheological response at large shear rates. Within this framework, we derive the critical shear rates by referencing coarse-grained coefficients representing an equivalent smectic phase with large effective shear viscosities. Theoretical results are shown to conform well with forthcoming experimental data.

Achieving a quantum advantage with near-term quantum devices depends crucially on efficient methods to boost the performance of currently available noisy hardware. In this study, we develop and experimentally confirm two high-efficiency error mitigation strategies, "Noiseless Output Extrapolation" and "Pauli Error Cancellation," designed to significantly improve the output of quantum circuits involving sequences of noisy gates. Our methods merge widelyused techniques—such as probabilistic error cancellation and noise amplification—with effective noise reconstruction algorithms. This combination allows mitigation across a broad spectrum of noise types, including complex, non-local, and gate-dependent processes that typically fall outside the reach of standard protocols. Using Advanced Quantum Testbeds four-qubit superconducting processor as our test case, we demonstrated enhanced circuit performance for both structured and random designs, achieving an $86\%$ improvement over unmitigated results using noise variation distance metrics. Our experiments confirm not only that these protocols are highly effective for reducing errors but also that they hold practical potential for deployment on modern quantum processing hardware.

Building on Orache et al.'s (2020) Kronecker product-based approach for Context-Free Path Queries (CFPQ), we simplify the method into Boolean matrix operations and enhance it to retrieve all relevant paths. This work presents an alternative to Chaudhuri's (2008) algorithm by utilizing a subcubic strategy grounded in linear algebra and incremental transitive closure rather than the original framework. Our assessment confirms the suitability of this method as a universal algorithm capable of handling both regular and context-free path inquiries efficiently.

Researchers in disaster response and humanitarian aid, alongside academics, rely on geospatial systems, though collaborating is hindered by distinct issues in both the nature of available data—ranging from variable-resolution multi-spectral images to weather patterns and time-series—to the diverse array of objectives, such as detecting forest fires. This research outlines a strategy to build a general-purpose neutral architecture infused with geospatial-specific biases that learns unsupervised concepts through massive, unlabelled earth observations. This model aims to serve as a catalyst for community cooperation, aiming to connect these previously disparate actors and enable them to operate more cohesively on common frontiers. Initial tests demonstrate that we instantiated a first-generation architecture capable of handling multiple mixed geospatial modalities, proving it holds competitive efficiency alongside specialized systems in areas pivotal to achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development goals.

Drawing inspiration from how geological structures evolve as the earth's crust bends due to magmatic intrusion, we explore elastohydrodynamic blister formation under an elastic layer. Integrating experiments, dimensional scaling, and computational modeling, we identify an emergent growth regime characterized by blister height increasing as $t^{5/9}$ and radius expanding as $t^{2/9}$. This blister dynamics is governed by plug-like flow, resulting in a quasi-static, self-similar geometry achieved when the pressure gradient generated by the bending elastic sheet balances the fluid's yield stress.

Determining the mutual orbital alignment in multi-planetary systems is crucial for understanding planet formation, often achieved through sophisticated photometric and spectroscopic methods like planet-planet occultations (PPOs). PPO events in multiple-transiting systems are particularly insightful; however, while detecting such an occultation constrains alignment, a system lacking PPO signals does not necessarily lack them if undetected. Systems that are difficult to probe with conventional obliquity measurements can now be better constrained by this novel approach. Our methodology extracts alignment information from multi-transit events in multi-planet configurations primarily using photometry. This process involves creating model light curves synthesized over a grid of projected axis inclinations ($\alpha$), holding standard transit parameters fixed, which effectively generates scenarios for potential occultations for specific geometric angles within our 3D Blender orbital simulation tools. By incorporating realistic surface brightness patterns, such as limb darkening modeled from stellar atmospheres, we generate flexible model curves to match observed light data. As a case study, we examine the Kepler-20 multi-transiting system, detailing planetary fit analysis and a breakdown of stellar noise influences. Applying this to Kepler-20b and 20c enabled the ruling out of several orbital configurations while identifying an apparent propensity for prograde eclipses across different stellar hemispheres.

Utilizing integral field spectroscopy from the Calar Alto Legacy Integral Field Area survey, we examined the stellar properties of bulge and disk regions within 34 intermediate (S0) galaxies individually. We simultaneously derived spatially resolved stellar ages and metallicities for these components using the penalized pixel fitting method, applying photometric weights specific to each region. Our findings reveal a tight age-to-metallicity correlation for S0 bulges, whereas the corresponding relationship for disks shows greater scatter, suggesting that disk star-forming histories are more intricate than those of bulges. High-metallicity similarity characterizes bulges of high-mass S0 galaxies; conversely, bulges of lower-mass S0 galaxies exhibit systematically higher metallicity than their disks. In high-mass S0 galaxies, bulge and disk stellar ages correlate positively with local density. Similarly, bulge ages in low-mass S0 galaxies increase with local density, though no clear such trend appears for disk ages in these systems. Furthermore, the age discrepancy between bulge and disk components (ΔAge) grows with local density across all mass categories. Interestingly, high-mass S0 galaxies display systematically larger ΔAge than their low-mass counterparts at equivalent local densities. These results affirm the influence of stellar mass on the evolutionary paths of S0 galaxies while confirming a critical role for the environment in shaping the development of both bulge and disk structures at fixed mass.

Although Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit human-like capabilities across many natural language tasks, it has remained largely unexamined whether their ability to internalize knowledge from structured formats like knowledge graphs (KGS) outperforms learning from unstructured text. Addressing this, our study introduces a direct training approach for the T5 architecture solely upon knowledge graph factual triples. Experiments demonstrate that models trained with our methodology using Wikidata surpass standard T5 baselines on FreebaseQA, WikiHop, and subsets of TriviaQA and NaturalQuestions where Wikidata provides answers. Furthermore, models trained exclusively on factual triples compete closely with those pre-trained on natural language counterparts encoding the same information. Evaluation on a smaller dataset, WikiMovies, revealed a threefold increase in exact match scores for the MetaQA benchmark relative to T5. A notable benefit of the proposed approach is that it eliminates the need for alignment efforts required to match a knowledge graph against corpus data during preparation, rendering the method especially advantageous for industry-scale knowledge graphs.

The inaugural "VIPriors" dataset competition, which explored using "Data-Efficient Deep Learning," presented five scenarios focused specifically on training data-constrained fundamental computer vision tasks. To stimulate innovation and the creation of novel inductive biases—thereby enhancing data efficiency—the organizers banned the use of pre-trained models and transfer learning methodologies. In every challenge, the winning submissions dramatically surpassed the established baselines, achieving these gains through advanced data augmentation strategies, extensive ensembling techniques, and novel architectures designed for efficient data usage, all while training exclusively without pretraining weights from scratch on reduced datasets.

We define $\mathcal{B}(d)$ as the space equipped with the Hausdorff metric consisting of all centrally symmetric convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Within this, $\mathcal{B}_\otimes(d_1,\dots,d_l)$ represents the subset of convex bodies formed by the closed unit balls of reasonable crossnorms on that tensor product space. Furthermore, we devised an innovative technique to synthesize data that mimicts the distribution of real-world selection datasets but maintains a verifiable ground-truth causal structure. We evaluated GnIES across synthetic, real, and our newly generated semi-synthetic datasets. Even though the methodology relies on strict Gaussian assumptions, it proves robust against multiple model violations and competitively recovers causal structures from small to large sample sizes. As free tools for GnIES and our sampling methodology, we offer Python libraries named gnIES and Seimler, respectively, providing accessible resources for causal inference.

Lifespan Face Synthesis (LFS) refers to a model that produces photo-realistic face images representing an individual's entire lifespan based solely on a single reference snapshot. Given a specific age code, the generated output aims to capture age-sensitive morphological and textural changes in a biologically realistic manner while maintaining the subject's unique identity. This task is highly challenging because facial shape and textures transform independently and in a highly nonlinear fashion as a person ages. Recent LFS approaches predominantly leverage Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), applying age-conditional adjustments to latent face representations. While benefiting from recent GAN advancements, these models lack the disentanglement of latent factors into distinct texture, shape, and identity components, fundamentally limiting their ability to effectively simulate nonlinear age-related texture and shape shifts while simultaneously preserving identity. To address this, we propose a new LFS model that explicitly disentangles essential facial characteristics. By extracting separate shapes, textures, and identity features within an encoder, our method independently models the distinct nonlinear aging processes for each trait. Specifically, we employ a conditional convolution module for texture transformations and a channel attention module for shape transformations. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art alternatives, with full code and demos accessible at https://senhe.github.io/projects/iccv_2021_2.0_lifespan_FACE/.

Locating Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) presents the enduring difficulty of determining the source direction. "Recently, Deep Learning has emerged as the dominant approach for Single-Image Super Resolution Reconstruction (SISR), demonstrating remarkable effectiveness. However, as SISR is a task plagued by intrinsic uncertainties, achieving high-quality reconstruction quickly with rich texture and detail simultaneously presents a significant challenge. This incompatibility often results in method failures characterized by collapsed outputs, loss of textural information in high-resolution (HR) reconstructions, and excessively slow generation times. To address these issues, we propose a Diffusion Probabilistic Model with Latent features (LDDPM). Initially, a Conditional Encoder is developed to effectively encode Low-Resolution (LR) inputs, constraining the solution space for the reconstructed images to enhance overall performance. Furthermore, by integrating Normalized Flows with Multi-modal GAN training, we model the denoising distribution to capture complex multi-modal characteristics, enabling enhanced generative capabilities even at a limited number of sampling steps. Empirical evaluation on major benchmark datasets reveals that our approach generates notably more realistic high-resolution reconstructions, surpassing existing SISR methods with improved PSNR and SSIM metrics, and offering a transformative perspective for future work in this area."

This study provides an analytic analysis regarding how pointing inaccuracies influence the average bit-error probability (ABEB) in optically amplified pulse-position modulation (PPM) systems. This study introduces a catalog comprising 991 candidate heartbeat star (HBS) systems drawn from the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE) archive, detailing both their identification process and organizational structure. This study introduces a new strategy for semi-supervised semantic segmentation, anchored by an innovative contrastive learning module. The significance of Machine Learning (ML) in everyday existence is deeply linked to its interpretability, which enables end-users to comprehend a machine-learning scheme transparently and ethically while bolstering their trust in automated determinations; revealing which variables justify a decision is increasingly essential. Optical pulling forces, commonly known as tractor beams, are capable of pulling objects opposite to the direction of light propagation. This phenomenon is typically generated using Bessel beams with narrow half-cone angles, a method often constrained by its limited applicability. However, this limitation can be bypassed by utilizing a superposition of plane waves. This research establishes a theoretical framework incorporating Mie theory, Debye potentials, and Wigner rotation matrices to examine forces exerted by non-collinear plane wave pairs against a metal-dielectric composite particle system. These composites emerge as an optimized alternative for tractor beam enhancement beyond simple homogeneous materials, as demonstrated to be superior for creating a strong pulling force between them via metallic element modifications, resulting force that reflects varying particle polarizations. These findings significantly improve optical trapping through flexible material optimization and provide an avenue to improve optical trapping forces to be more applicable.

**Methods:** This study employs Bayesian analysis alongside Monte Carlo (MC) sampling to assess how photospheric composition and touchdown radius impact LMXBs exhibiting PREs across radio-to-soft X-ray bands (RX). This study investigates the shift from tensile failure caused by necking to failure caused by shear-banding in metallic glasses. The transition moves from high temperatures or low strain rates toward lower temperatures or higher strain rates. By combining large tensile tests on metallic glasses with atomic-level simulations, we demonstrate a sequence of macroscopic failure modes parameterized by ultimate tensile strength. Our analysis, supported by fracture surface analysis, examines how the interaction between shear-induced plastic deformation and expansion-driven cavity formation (cavitation) governs these different outcomes before failure. Specifically, we found that the ultimate size of the cavity forming in the load direction at failure is a non-linear function of temperature. These findings are interpreted through the balance between shear and dilation driven plastic flow, alongside a correlation linking the cavity size to the undeformed cross-sectional surface area. These results shed new light on the tension fracture mechanism and show that current glass models must integrate constitutive concepts involving both shear and volume expansion processes.

The universal schema (USchema) posits sentence pattern similarity whenever two patterns contain identical entity pairs; however, this assumption is frequently violated because each pattern comprises multiple facets, not all of which align with corresponding facets from another pattern sharing the same entity pair. While commonly utilized in diverse relation extraction (RE) tasks, this approach overlooks such discrepancies. Consequently, we propose a multi-facet USchema enhanced with a neural model. Our method represents every sentence pattern through diverse facet embeddings rather than relying on a single vector, explicitly enforcing proximity between compatible embeddings across patterns associated with matching entities. Experimental evidence demonstrates the superiority of these multi-facet representations over both traditional single-facet alternatives such as compositional USchema (CUSchema) and their performance on distantly supervised Re tasks. Furthermore, this multi-embedding approach facilitates the identification of entailment relations without the requirement of manually provided labels, offering the added insight of verifying logical relationships simply through shared sentences that utilize identical multi-face representations of related words within their sentence context.

Thus, we have demonstrated not only how to address non-trivial cases of sentence pattern confusion also but how to solve distantly supervised Re tasks by leveraging complex structure underlying textual patterns instead of relying only on simple cooccurrences or assuming full similarity without careful consideration.

The aim of physical-layer security (PLS) resides in leveraging specific characteristics of the wireless channel and transceiver components to facilitate vital elements of secure transmission, namely message integrity, node authentication, and dataset confidentiality. Distinct from classical methods relying on computational hardness, PLS offers inherent quantum resistance by relying on information-theoretic security principles that remain effective regardless of an adversary's computational capacity. This survey examines these core PLS concepts chronologically: it begins with node authentication and shifts toward an information-theoretic analysis of message integrity, concluding with message confidentiality strategies involving shared-randomness secret keys and wiretap channel models. The paper's objective is to outline a comprehensive guide to relevant literature, highlighting key findings and addressing unresolved challenges concerning PLS integration in sixth-generation (6G) network architectures.

Before data mining and machine learning processes, swarm optimization algorithms play a critical role in feature selection, though their use of natural-inspired, single-objective heuristics often leads to premature convergence, thereby limiting their effectiveness. By integrating Bee Swarm Optimization (BSO) with Reinforcement Learning (RL), RSO enhances performance through a mechanism that rewards superior search agents and penalizes underperforming ones. Consequently, this hybrid approach offers superior adaptability and robustness while maintaining an optimal balance between exploration and exploitation. Our method's efficacy was validated on 25 standard UCI datasets, encompassing both balanced and imbalanced data distributions when compared against several other established feature selection algorithms. In 22 out of 25 instances (88%), the proposed model outperformed basic BSO, and it achieved the highest performance across 19 of the 25 cases (76%) compared to all benchmark methods, demonstrating its distinct superiority.

Synergistic drug combinations offer immense promise for boosting therapeutic outcomes and minimizing adverse effects; however, predicting such combinations effectively and synergistically remains an unsolved problem due to the elusiveness of causal disease mechanisms. We validated the performance of SANEpool using molecular data from 46 core cancer pathways alongside drug combination benchmarks from the NCI ALMANAC dataset. Empirical results demonstrate two main achievements: SANEpool matches or exceeds the performance of other leading graph neural networks, and the sub-networks it identifies are both intuitively clear and highly effective for flagging synergistic drug regimens.

This paper introduces the task of language-guided semantic style transfer for 3D indoor scenes. Taking a 3D indoor scene mesh along with text descriptions describing the desired style as input, our approach operates through a pipeline. First, a multi-layer perceptron maps 3D vertex coordinates to RGB colors. Subsequently, a viewpoint-specific sampling method adapted for indoor environments is employed to differentiably render these colored 4D meshes into 2D images. We then compare these rendered 2D views against textual prompts using pre-trained vision-language models to generate error signals, which are back-propagated to the perceptron to adjust vertex-by-color levels based on specific semantics. Extensive qualitative evaluations and A/B user tests using the public ScanNet and SceneNN datasets reveal four key insights: (1) The method produces aesthetically pleasing outcomes with practical value for multimedia; (2) Rendering 3D indoor scenes from camera angles that align with human viewpoint priors proves critical. (3)  Integrating semantic information markedly enhances style-transfer accuracy. (4) Including an HSV regularization term ensures higher consistency and yields superior ratings. Source code and the accompanying tools are available via the Lightning.

Logic locking is a critical method for safeguarding the integrity of hardware designs during IC design and manufacturing. Recently, however, the vulnerability of these locking schemes has escalated due to novel deobfuscation attacks. Alongside these advances, the field of security research has increasingly integrated deep learning approaches. This paper introduces **SnapShot**, the pioneering logic locking attack that employs artificial neural networks to predict specific key bits directly from a synthesized, locked gate-level netlist, operating without access to a Golden reference. SnapShot leverages a streamlined yet highly adaptable model compared to prior solutions by evaluating two distinct strategies: a simple fully connected feed-forward neural network and a second method that utilizes genetic algorithms to evolve complex Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) specifically optimized for this detection task. This attack provides a generalizable, customizable framework for employing machine learning against various locking schemes. We rigorously evaluated SnapShot under two practical scenarios involving standard reference benchmarks and silicon-found silicon RISC-V modules, specifically with no reference provided. Results indicate SnapShot attains an average key prediction accuracy of 82.60%, representing a notable 10.49 percentage-point superiority over the state-of-the-art. Furthermore, the tool exceeds current techniques on all benchmarks. These findings suggest that existing logic locking schemes rely on flawed assumptions regarding security. Consequently, the study provides valuable guidance on the challenges necessary for developing future logic locking implementations resistant to machine learning-based attacks.

We begin by clarifying adiabaticity for non-Hermitian systems, demonstrating that realizable state adiabaticity necessitates a real energy spectrum. Consequently, achieving an exact transition to a specific eigenstate via counterdiabatic driving either requires a real energy spectrum or mandates omitting components of the dynamic phase and geometric (Berry) phase. Guided by this framework, we formulate explicit counterdiabatic Hamiltonians and adiabatic criteria for Hamiltonians that are pseudo-Hermitian with either real or complex energy spectra, and those which are ant pseudo-Hermitian with either imaginary or complex energy spectra. We validate these theoretical findings through a detailed study of counterdiabatic control in a specific three-level non-Hermitian system, where we successfully achieve perfect population transfer accompanied by controlled loss.

Capturing faces of vehicle occupants from within the cabin via windshields presents significant difficulties in unstructured settings due to factors like reflections, inadequate lighting, head orientation, and motion-induced blurring. This study enhances both the hardware and software elements of a bespoke automobile imaging system to mitigate these obstacles. This paper evaluates design principles that should be adhered to when architecting a similar open-source software package repository.

Current datasets for deep learning-based narrowband radio frequency (RF) signal classification are inadequate due to insufficient variety in signal categories and channel degradations, limiting their effectiveness in real-world validation. This work presents Sig53, a comprehensive repository comprising 5 million synthetic samples across 53 signal classes and a selection of artificially induced impairments selected by experts. Alongside Sig53, we release TorchSig, a signaling processing machine learning framework capable of generating such datasets; it adopts practices common to the vision field and is designed as an open-source cornerstone for forthcoming signal-based machine learning endeavors. Early trials leveraging Sig53 employed state-of-the-art ConvNets alongside Transformers, revealing that Transformers surpass ConvNets performance without requiring extra regularization or guidance from ConvNet teachers—a finding that diverges from trends observed in vision tasks. Further tests confirm that TorchSig's specialized data augmentation techniques enhance training efficiency and boost overall model efficacy. Additionally, TorchSig facilitates real-time, on-the-fly synthetic data synthesis during training, thereby supporting extensive-scale training procedures with effectively limitless data capacity.

This work explores a distinct "reduction" strategy for achieving "un-reduction." It involves mapping systems originating from Lagrange systems on manifolds to equivalent D.S.'s residing on principal bundles, where solutions are properly projected. Demonstrating that the former can indeed be framed in the guise of secondary-degree ordinary differential systems (SODEs), we present how these "primary" versions are linked to other forms. Finally, we leverage illustrative cases to show how the proposed procedure transcends classical Lagrangian frameworks as per current literature.

The Colorado Ultraviolet Transit Experiment (CUTE) functions as a NASA 6U CubeSat equipped with an onboard low-resolution spectrograph operating in the near-UV spectrum (2479-3306 Ångströms). To address spatial restrictions imposed by its specific bus design, the satellite utilizes a Cassegrain telescope featuring a rectangular primary mirror, combined with an aberration-correcting grating to enhance spectral resolution. Since its deployment on September 27, 2021, to Low Earth Orbit, the mission's objectives involve observing transits of exoplanets around accessible, luminous stars to study planetary atmospheric escape and star-planet interaction dynamics. This document details COUNTER, an autonomous autonomous data Reduction, acquired OnOrbit Real-time Line-scope, and Temporal Analysis (CONTROL)—a pipeline engineered specifically for CUTE's data processing. Built with a modular architecture, the system ensures both extensibility across CUBE-Sats and ease of transfer to missions utilizing onboard long-slit spectrographs. Development and testing leveraged synthetic observations produced by a CUTE simulator, with subsequent refinement applied using nine hours of data collected during the mission's commissioning and preliminary science phases.

While Strongly-coupled Quantum Field Theories (QFTs) are fundamental across many-body and high-energy physics, performing accurate calculations within these systems remains challenging. The Hamiltonian Truncation technique overcomes this by numerically integrating real-time nonperturbative evolution via the Schrödinger equation on a restricted subset of the full Hilbert space, applicable to continuum-limit QFTs. Significant recent developments in refining this approach have revitalized various fields, spanning gauge theories across $d\ge2$ dimensions to relativistic nonequilibrium phenomena.

This research investigates scenarios involving several nondeterministically missing predictors alongside incomplete outcome measurements. Our study establishes a novel framework capable of addressing intricate patterns of missing data in predictors through the use of inverse probability weighting, regression stratification, and a robust methodology. This framework is utilized to solve three fundamental problems: survival time analysis utilizing the Cox proportional hazards model, imputation for missing responses, and causal effect inference with unobserved treatments in binary settings. Furthermore, we examine the treatment of absent covariates within these contexts by establishing corresponding theoretical identifiability conditions and asymptotic properties. Practical validation is achieved through simulation studies based on the framework as applied to real data from studies of cognitive disorders (Alzheimer's disease).

This summary outlines contemporary progress in pulsar halo research, covering source definitions, confirmed examples, candidate models for the observed diffusion anomalies, their utility as cosmological probes, insights into particle injections from PBNe generated PWNe—and their implications regarding unresolved cosmic positron and TeV radiation anomalies. Lastly, we anticipate fostering progress in predicting a more abundant array of observable pulsed halos utilizing more profound observations.

Image matting involves estimating the alpha channel for unknown foreground pixels within natural scenes. Existing techniques primarily propagate alpha estimates from known to unknown regions but fail when objects lack a specifically identified foreground, a common issue with transparent elements such as glass or web. Our approach reformulates the standard trimap into three learnable token sources, injecting advanced semantic cues directly into the self-attention mechanism, and deploys a lightweight convolution module for guiding multi-scale feature propagation between the decoder and encoder using both non-background masking and global context, thereby preserving fine structural details. Additionally, we have established a new high-resolution benchmark for transparency matting, characterised by minimal or non-existent annotated foreground areas. Comparative experiments across various standard matsing datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

Humans are uniquely able to detect unfamiliar instances while utilizing prior acquired knowledge to differentiate unknowns. Notably, they accomplish this without compromising the performance attributed to previously acquired insights. Guided by this inherent human trait and acknowledging current limitations in addressing these exacting problems with models that prioritize only classification accuracy, we formalized and defined the pragmatic problem setting: Novel Class Discovery without Forgetting (NCDwF). This task mandates incremental learning by machine models based on discovering novel instance clusters in unlabeled data, which the model is unable to categorize while remaining uninformed by the categories seen prior.

Furthermore, our method: a) generates pseudo-latent representations serving as a direct approximation for labels about which the model is unaware and that are not available for training to diminish forgetting and loss of insights across various trained categories using only newly acquired instances; b) utilizes regularizer-based approaches using mutual information to fortify unsupervised learning capabilities while identifying new categories to maintain past information in the model architecture; c) utilizes an efficient and straightforward known-class identifier to achieve generalized cross-category results while remaining adaptable. Additionally, we have conducted a suite of experimental protocols across diverse data sets, specifically CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1000, and related implementations. Empirics suggest that these results improve upon existing models which exhibit critical deficiencies where they indiscriminately forget previously acquired knowledge to achieve improved performance when interpreting novel instances simultaneously. Our contributions hope to inspire further investigations into the pragmatic challenges associated with these identified problems in novel class identification paradigms within machine learning environments.

Hall-Effect Thrusters (HETs) are currently essential for near-Earth spacecraft propulsion and are crucial advancements for future deepspace exploration. It is well understood that image classifiers powered by neural networks are easily fooled by adversarial images created through subtle perturbation. When successfully implemented, traditional unilateral adversarial objectives may fail to uncover the specific adversarial inputs due the small size and intricate designs of the crafted perturbations. As a consequence of such optimizations, we find that pure image de-noise models may overcorrect the reconstruction loss, but generally lose the key underlying class distribution. To solve this challenge, we offer the principled reverse engineering (Rethinking Deception and Recovery - RED) protocol to achieve generalizable techniques primarily based on the prediction homogenization in terms of data synthesis (such as spatial transformations), which are crucial components for generalizing deep adversarial networks. By incorporating these principles into existing de-noise models, we introduce the novel Class-dictionary Discriminative De-noise framework, termed CDD-Rethinking Deception and Recovery (RDD). Extensive experiments prove that it is effective across all three evaluation tiers—from pixel-level and prediction-level generalizations up to high-level attribute alignment, testing various adversarial generation attacks, such as FSGPS and CW, along with their Adaptive variations and robust AutoAttack.

Over the past ten years, person re-identification (Person Re-ID) has been a prominent research focus driven by its practical value and theoretical potential. Although supervised Person Re-ID methods outperform unsupervised ones, they struggle to scale to vast unlabelled datasets or new domains because of the prohibitive cost of annotation, leading to rising interest in unsupervised Person Re-ID due to its scalability benefits. However, this unsupervised variant faces inherent difficulty primarily because of the absence of identity labels necessary to supervise feature learning. Various solutions exist to address this, each carrying distinct merits and drawbacks. Given the landscape of methods involved, comprehensive surveys are vital for articulating challenges and strategies to stimulate future advancements. While prior Person Re-ID surveys often cover supervised techniques through classifications and applications, they frequently lack deep analysis of the underlying challenges their proposed solutions tackle. In contrast, this survey reviews recent unsupervised Person Re-ID works by examining both the associated challenges and the corresponding resolutions. Specifically, it examines influential methods through four key hurdles: (1) the scarcity of ground-truth labels to supervise feature learning, (2) acquiring discriminative features via pseudo-label guidance, (3) ensuring camera-invariance across different scenes, and (4) handling domain shifts between datasets. The review evaluates and synthesizes effectiveness based on reported metrics and provides perspectives on solution efficiency. Finally, it highlights open problems and identifies promising avenues for future research.

Neural networks are frequently over-parameterized, making them susceptible to aggressive regularization techniques. Traditional methods like weight decay and standard Dropout fail to capitalize on the intrinsic structures inherent to network inputs and hidden states, resulting in reduced efficacy compared to structurally informed approaches such as SpatialDropout and DropBlock. The latter methods address this by zeroing out values within specific contiguous regions; however, the spatial configurations of these techniques remain manual, static patterns with random execution locations rather than adaptive designs. Empirical evaluations demonstrate robust effectiveness for image classification on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet as well as language modeling on Penn Treebank and WikiText-2. Furthermore, the derived dropout policies exhibit transfer learning capabilities across distinct datasets and domains, successfully migrating strategies from Penn Treebank linguistic tasks to English-French translation on the WMT 2014 dataset. Fabricated and machine-deceptive content poses severe risks to contemporary society, including within Arab nations, thus spurring research into identifying false or altered online narratives. Yet, this field struggles due to a scarcity of data for model training. We propose a streamlined approach to automatically synthesize Arabic manipulated news, requiring only authentic articles—which abound online—and a parts-of-speech tagger. To streamline future endeavors, we introduce AraNews, an extensive, ready-to-use POS-tagged Arabic news corpus, effectively removing prior dependencies. Leveraging stories crafted using this dataset, we conduct human evaluations to analyze the impact of automated alteration on textual authenticity and to gauge human proficiency in spotting our generated machine-manipulated content. Consequently, we create pioneer models for identifying fabricated Arabic news, achieving state-of-the-art performance with a macro F1 score of 70.06. Additionally, our generated models and the accompanying dataset are accessible to the public.

A binary phylogenetic network for a taxon set $X$ is defined as a rooted acyclic digraph with exactly three-degree nodes except for the leaves, which are uniquely labeled with the taxa in one-to-one correspondence. Such a network is termed "tree-child" if every non-leaf node possesses at least one child having an incoming edge from only a single parent. Although a collection of binary phylogenetic trees may not always fit into such a network simultaneously, this text outlines necessary conditions that must be met for it. Notably, any two distinct trees on a given taxon set can always be represented together within some tree-child network. Furthermore, any set of multiple binary phylogenetic trees can be simultaneously depicted within a non-binary tree-child network over the same taxon set. In these non-binary networks, every non-leaf node either maintains an incoming edge from one and an outgoing pair of edges or receives input from at least two while having an outgoing pair.

Generative Adversarial Networks are uniquely suited for precisely capturing the distribution of intricate, high-dimensional data like images, thereby making advanced GANs valuable for unsupervised anomaly detection in medical imaging. However, discrepancies in training datasets, including image output size and the representation of semantically relevant features, mean natural images models often require adaptation before application to medical tasks rather than working directly. This study adapts and evaluates three architectures—specifically DCGAN, styleGAN, and bigGAN—for modeling 3D healthy patches from pulmonary CT scans. This represents, to our knowledge, the inaugural evaluation combining these specific methods in a 3D pulmonary context. The selection of these models stems from their widespread popularity and superior performance in natural image processing sectors. Various iterations were trained, with success metrics including the Frechet Inception Distance (FID) score and a concurrent human perception study. Furthermore, the analysis assessed the modeling of domain-specific features in three dimensions and the organization of the latent spaces. The findings reveal a distinct strength of the modified styleGAN: it produces hyper-realistic, structurally coherent 3D images although it struggles with severe mode collapse that impedes sample diversity if left unresolved. The 3D DCGAN variants conversely, exhibit superior variability but generate significantly lower quality images. The intermediate 3D bigGAN architecture achieved a middle range regarding overall visual quality but outperformed the others by accurately representing distributions in key semantically meaningful features. Collectively, the study concludes that further advancement is needed before a 3D GAN possesses adequate capacity for chest CT anomaly detection at the patch level and offers specific guidance for prospective research, including testing alternative architectures and integrating position-encoding mechanisms.

Recently, Few-Shot Learning (FSL) has garnered significant attention, particularly metric-based methods that train embedding networks to cluster similar samples while pushing dissimilar ones apart, achieving notable success. FSL relies on limited sample images to build models capable of generalizing to unfamiliar classes in image recognition, yet sample size constraints complicate the learning of robust visual features necessary to handle intra-class appearances. Additionally, training can be misguided because objects within a single semantic class often display diverse appearances, whereas items across different classes might visually resemble one another. We posit that FSL could improve by incorporating semantic features to derive discriminative representations. Consequently, this study introduces a multi-task learning framework that utilizes the semantics of label text as an auxiliary objective to enhance FSL performance. Our model employs word-embeddings to capture semantic features for training the embedding network and integrates a semantic cross-attention mechanism to effectively align these features with standard visual inputs. Although the proposed architecture remains straightforward, it delivers superior results and, when integrated into two existing metric-based FSL frameworks significantly boosts their performance. The source code for our method is available publicly via GitHub.

First, we provide a complete structural description of strings from which unique reconstruction (allowing for reversal) fails based solely on their full multiset of prefix-suffix compositions. Utilizing this framework, we demonstrate that for every $n\ge 6$, a non-uniquely reconstructible string of that length exists. Furthermore, we explicitly construct the set of all length-$n$ strings for $n\ge 6$ that admit unique reversal-resolvable reconstruction. As an additional result, we show that any binary string can be generated using Dyck and Catalan-Berland strings. For any specific string $\bm{s}$, we define a procedure to build the set of all strings sharing $\bm{s}$’s prefix-suffix multiset, alongside corresponding counts for this set. As an applied consequence, we develop a code of maximal composition size, while also introducing two distinct classes of such codes capable of correcting specific composition errors involving missing elements (loss errors) and mass reduction (corruption errors). Finally, we propose two novel challenges: retrieving a string from its compositional multiset with only a bounded loss of substring compositions, and retrieving a string from its substring compositions constrained to lengths at most $r$. We present relevant codes contingent upon certain conditions to address each of these new scenarios.

Optimization challenges centered on locating the global minimum of a specified cost function occupy a core position in science and engineering. While numerous numerical approaches exist, Gradient Descent (GD) remains the most widespread because of its inherent simplicity and efficiency, though it is hindered by susceptibility to local minima and slow convergence rates near those optima. In contrast, Natural Gradient Descent (NGD) has demonstrated exceptional efficacy across diverse fields such as machine learning, tensor networks, and variational quantum algorithms by providing a means to accelerate convergence effectively. This study presents a unified framework that broadens the NGD approach to generalize scenarios while maintaining rapid convergence; this is achieved via the construction of an appropriate reference Riemannian manifold that identifies a suitable metric. This advancement extends beyond standard NGD and may illuminate broader insights into optimization strategies.

Deep gap electronic states created by crystal imperfections within a semiconductor's band gap often undermine its optoelectronic suitability; materials prone to avoiding these defect-induced levels are classified as "defect tolerant." This paper presents a systematic first-principles examination of defect tolerance across 29 monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) promising for nanoscale applications. Our findings indicate that TMDs involving Group IV metals exhibit only shallow defect states characteristic of defect tolerance, conversely, those relying on Group V/VI metals develop deep gap levels when experiencing chalcogen (S, Se, Te) vacancies. Notably, defect-sensitive TMDs display valence and conduction band structures with comparable orbital characteristics, pointing toward a specific bonding/anti-bonding configuration of the gap where dangling states reside internally. A new quantitative descriptor measuring the similarity between conduction and valence manifolds formalizes these observations. Finally, we extend the investigation to non-polar TMD nanoribbons, observing that only inherently defect-prone materials exhibit intra-gap edge states.

Recent large-scale, dual-stream pretraining, exemplified by CLIP, leveraging vast volumes of image-text pairs has demonstrated superior performance across a variety of multimodal alignment tasks. This study addresses solving discounted Markov Decision Processes (MDMs) with the requirement that the resulting policy remains stabilizing. Although stability theory for MPC is currently most robust in undiscounted scenarios, this paper reformulates stable discounted MDPs as undiscounted equivalents first. We investigate complex-valued scaling, a unique symmetry inherent to complex-valued measurements and representations. While existing Deep Complex Networks (DCNs) extend real algebra to the complex realm without accounting for complex-valued scaling, SurvReal imposes a restricted manifold perspective using a distance metric; this achieves scaling invariance but sacrifices rich complex-valued data. Additionally, we introduce complex-valued RGB representations where such scaling reflects hue shifts or correlated changes across channels. Empirically evaluated on MSTAR, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and SVHN datasets, our co-domain symmetric (CDS)-based classifiers outperform both DCN and Surreal models, offering improved accuracy, generalization, and resilience to co-domain transformations, while simultaneously exhibiting lower bias, variance, and a significantly reduced parameter count.

Deep Neural Networks typically employ iterative gradient descent for training. However, gradient magnitudes are contingent on various elements like activation functions and parameter initialization. Most critically, gradient magnitudes can vary significantly between layers, resulting in slower updates for layers subjected to minimal gradients. Such disparity retards the overall training convergence. To address this, our approach analyzationally clarifies this uneven scaling. We propose equalizing the update speed across layers by scaling weights inversely proportional to their current L1 norms during gradient calculation for all learnable parameters in the network.

Experiments on MNIST demonstrate our method achieves relative changes in the norm of tensors consistent across layers throughout optimization. Compared existing approaches, training using our technique yields faster accuracy gains at the same step budget and eventually better test performance, as measured against time and steps respectively.

Inspired by research examining how progesterone levels fluctuate relative to menstrual cycle days, this paper introduces a novel multi-kink quantile regression model tailored for longitudinal analyses. This approach relaxes standard linear constraints by accommodating distinct functional relationships at various segments defined by threshold covariates. Specifically, we detail a multi-kink framework for longitudinal settings and present two strategies for estimating regression coefficients and locating kink points: a computationally streamlined profile estimation method based on an assumption of working independence, and a second technique employing unbiased generalized estimation equations to capture intra-subject correlations. Furthermore, we demonstrate the consistency in kink selection and the asymptotic normality of both estimators, and we formulate a rank-score test using partial subgradients to detect kink presence, deriving its null and alternative distribution properties in the context of longitudinal data. Simulation experiments confirm robust performance in finite samples. Application to actual menstrual cycle data successfully identifies two inflection points, revealing that progesterone remains constant pre-ovulatory, rises sharply during the subsequent five to six days, and eventually stabilizes again or declines slightly.

We introduce the Multivariate Quantile Function Forecaster (MQF$^2$), a global probabilistic modeling technique based on multivariate quantile functions, with a specific investigation into multi-horizon forecasting. Existing methods generally fall into two categories: autoregressive models that inherently track temporal dependencies but suffer from compounded errors over longer horizons, or multi-horizon sequence-to-sequence models which stabilize against error accumulation yet typically fail to explicitly capture time-step dependencies. MQF$^2$ merges the strengths of these approaches by predicting output directly as a multivariate quantile function. This function is defined by optimizing and parametric modeling of the gradient applied to convex functions utilizing neural architectures that input-strictly allow convex optimization. Since our method produces quantile functions, we ensure monotonicity with respect to input levels, thereby preventing quantile crossing issues. Additionally, we present two training strategies using both maximum likelihood and energy score objectives. Empirical validation across realistic and artificial data demonstrates that MQF$^2$ rivals leading methods in single-time-step precision while successfully modeling intricate temporal structures.

Algorithmic recourse aims to flip adverse decisions in automated systems, such as converting a loan rejection into an approval, by proposing feasible feature adjustments like reducing the credit card count. Most existing approaches for achieving cost-effective recourse operate on the Independent and Mutually Fake feature assumption (IMF) regarding feature manipulation, while others tackle feature dependencies through causal models. Yet, relying heavily on causal models often limits their use in intricate settings where cause-and-effect structures are unclear. To resolve this tension, we propose \texttt{DEAR} (DisEntangling Algorithmic Recourse), a new framework that harmonizes the IMF assumption with strong causal constraints designed for the IMF's limitations. By extracting a refined subset of high-value recourse options from latent encodings of interdependent features, \texttt{DEAR} better aligns with essential requirements for actionable interventions. Empirical results based on real-world data validate this theoretical approach yet demonstrating \texttt{DEAR} provides dependable and economically efficient recourses even when feature dependencies are complex.

A substantial spike in cloud resource utilization can degrade service availability, leading to outages, resource bottlenecks, and increased power consumption. A novel parameter, VM significance ranking, is calculated for each instance based on its critical task execution, enabling the selection of an appropriate High Availability strategy aligned with user constraints. Evaluated via experiments using the Google Cluster dataset, SRE-HM was benchmarked against state-of-the-art methods. By dynamically adjusting class-specific thresholds at every training step, CPL facilitates the incorporation of highly informative unlabeled data along with their corresponding pseudo-labels. Notably, CPL introduces no additional parameters or computational costs regarding gradient flow. We integrate CPL into the FixMatch algorithm, naming our refined method **FlexMatch**.
